transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Kuwait says Iranian drones attacked what it's calling a vital site in the country.
NPR's Ayyeb Etrawi reports Tehran,
which has openly acknowledged past attacks on its Gulf neighbors,
says it was not behind this one.
Kuwait says Iranian drones attacked a vital site in the country,
killing two Italians and wounding two other people.
Italy's Foreign Ministry says the Italian men were civilian technicians
working for defense company Rheinmetall.
Italy says they were working on maintenance of air defense systems
used by Kuwait's armed forces.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Iraqchi held calls with his counterparts
in Kuwait and Italy after Thursday's attack,
saying his country had "no role" in the incident.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard also issued a statement saying it was not behind the attack.
Iran last openly targeted U.S. military sites in Kuwait about a week ago,
saying it was in response to U.S. attacks on an island in the Strait of Hormuz.
There are no indications of similar attacks since.
Ayyeb Etrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is set to go before the Senate Banking Committee next week
during a hearing on U.S. export controls.
He's also expected to meet with three House committees behind closed doors.
NVIDIA's board reinstated Huang on Monday.
President Trump was asked about the decision last night
while taking questions from reporters at Mar-a-Lago.
Without him, I just don't know.
You know, everybody's replaceable, I guess,
but I just thought I saw that what was happening with the company,
what was happening with the stock.
And I think it's a great thing that he's going back.
Huang stepped down earlier this month amid reports they had an affair
with a woman who U.S. officials say had contact with Chinese intelligence.
Lawmakers want to know whether Chinese companies got access
to advanced NVIDIA chips barred from export to China.
Millions of dollars were spent on campaign ads generated
or enhanced by artificial intelligence this cycle.
They didn't appear to affect the outcome of the midterm elections,
but campaigns are likely to use more of them in the future.
NPR's Maham Javed reports.
At least $187 million was spent during the midterms
on ads that used A.I., according to the nonpartisan Wesleyan Media Project.
Experts say the ads didn't connect with many voters in this cycle.
But as the technology gets better, the ads will become more convincing.
And it'll be harder to detect what is real, says Brian Riddle, a GOP strategist.
It's not just about convincing some people that fake things are real.
Sometimes it's about people thinking that real things are now fake.
Riddle says the A.I. ads are also cheaper,
making them especially attractive for down-ballot candidates.
Maham Javed, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Voters in Spain go to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is fighting to stay in office
eight years into his time in power.
Sánchez called the election when lawmakers rejected his proposals
to tackle Spain's housing crisis.
The latest polls put the Conservative People's Party on track to win the most seats.
The final results of the election in New Zealand have failed to produce an outright winner.
The ruling right-wing coalition fell short of a parliamentary majority by just one seat
and will need support from a new centrist party to form government.
Christina Kukula reports from Melbourne.
Preliminary results from the November 7 vote gave the bloc,
led by New Zealand's National Party,
to narrow a lead to declare victory over the centre-left Labour Party.
Now the final count, which includes votes from overseas,
confirms the incumbent party and its two coalition partners
have won 65 of 130 seats in Parliament.
To form a government, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will need to secure support
from the brand new unaligned Opportunity Party.
Luxon ruled out working with Opportunity before the election
and now concedes negotiations may be challenging and could take some time.
If he fails, New Zealand may have to hold a new election.
For NPR News, I'm Christina Kukula in Melbourne, Australia.
Gas prices in the US are averaging around $3.55 for a gallon of regular,
according to AAA that's down from about $3.69 a week ago.
This is NPR News in Washington.
That's plus dot NPR dot org.

topics.text: Kuwait says Iranian drones attacked a vital site, killing two Italian civilian technicians
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang set to testify before Senate Banking Committee on export controls
Millions spent on AI-generated or enhanced campaign ads in midterms, per Wesleyan Media Project
Spain holds early parliamentary election Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez fights to stay in office
New Zealand election yields no outright winner; Luxon's coalition one seat short of majority
US gas prices average about $3.55 per gallon, down from $3.69 a week ago
